original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Replace the inherited H2/K (and literal H4) interface by a twisted contract: frame-zero, source-free D may leave the helpers in any invertible helper-only state T, provided C U' (I_x ⊕ T) = I on z and N = K'T. Prove it, exhibit one precisely specified helper-mixing word (three helper-star restorations of the PR1062 and PR1188 words absorbed into A gates before the centres' first reads) with full dirty boundary, unchanged frame paths and paid profile, and run an exhaustive single-edge single-writer census on the PR967, PR1062, PR1122 and PR1188 words.
scope_change_reason: PR1194 and PR1311 already cover the T = I semantic-D replacement for words whose D restores every helper. This package narrows, as the card allows, to one helper-star absorption class and weakens the contract further to unrestored (twisted) helpers, which the absorbed words need. It does not attempt hosted adoption, native replay or a global optimum.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the bit supplier. A legitimate replacement interface admits a cheaper helper-mixing word (3 complete ADDs fewer) with an unchanged paid profile and rank mass, so the selected moment and kappa are unchanged; the bit side does not bind.
stop_rule: Stop after the twisted lemma, the two fixed instances, the single-edge single-writer census on four lineage words and the seven controls; no multi-gate search, native replay or hosted emission.
evidence: EXPECTED.json, PROOF.md, absorbed-pr1062.json.gz and absorbed-pr1188.json.gz; python3 -I -B research/r439-twisted-star-absorption-seed02/verify.py prints PASS_R439_TWISTED_STAR_ABSORPTION.
author: Sagar Thakrar
ai_assistance: Prepared by Sagar Thakrar with substantial Anthropic Claude assistance (Claude Code, including subagents for the exploratory probes and package assembly). No independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can a helper-star restoration be absorbed by splitting its substitute set across two or more centre writers, or by chaining one of the gain-0 neutral moves (120 on the PR1062 word, two of them path-preserving) with a positive move?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The census is exhaustive only for one deleted restoration and one edited gate; multi-gate absorption could admit further frame-legal savings under the same twisted contract.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the census to two-writer splits of S before the first centre read, with the same frame-path filter.
open_questions.blocked_by: Search budget only; the candidate space grows quadratically in the centre writers per edge.

open_questions.question: Do the absorbed words pass the native 5/9/11-stage C++ checkers that PR1122 and PR1188 ran on their base words?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package checks local scalar, frame and precision facts only; native multistage replay is the next layer of evidence.
open_questions.first_step: Run the PR1188 native checkers on absorbed-pr1188.json.gz with Boost, or with open PR #1509's checked cpp_int stand-in.
open_questions.blocked_by: A host with Boost headers or an accepted stand-in; not run here.

open_questions.question: Do target-feedback or shear savings appear once the helper exit may be twisted (T != I) and absorbed by C?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR1706 (with PR1306 and PR1557) finds no feedback saving for fully restored dirty shears, the T = I case; the twisted contract enlarges that model.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun the 3-by-3 shear census allowing any helper exit T in GL(R,2) and charge the C absorption.
open_questions.blocked_by: A cost convention for the C absorption that is consistent with the scalar shear model.

open_questions.question: Will maintainers accept the twisted contract, together with the helper common-frame/climb-additivity premise, as an interface for hosted admission?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Without acceptance the absorbed words remain scoped finite constructions, not supplier candidates.
open_questions.first_step: Review PROOF.md section 4 against the inherited chronological lemma and PR1194's frame-zero restriction.
open_questions.blocked_by: Maintainer decision, then a hosted emission and invoice of an absorbed word.
